verdict.rationale: Figma Make's own docs say you can describe a backend in chat and Make will create a Payload-powered backend that includes a database. Make then updates the data model and interface together, and publishing deploys the backend to Figma's hosted infrastructure, all inside the builder. A Supabase project can also be connected from Make settings. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that provisioning works as claimed, and documentation of the database engine, migrations or limits.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get a database provisioned and wired into my app without leaving the builder

citations.quote: Describe what you want to build in the chat, and Make can create a Payload-powered backend, including a database, file storage, authentication, and an admin panel.
Make updates the data model and the interface to support the new fields.
Publishing deploys your app and its Payload backend to Figma’s hosted infrastructure.
You can also manually connect a Supabase project from Make settings.
